summary: Install-time host-identification beacon to OOB collectors
details: @myorder-frontend-commons/analytics@1.1.0 declares preinstall, install, and postinstall lifecycle scripts in package.json that all execute `node poc.js`. On any `npm install`, poc.js collects host identifiers (os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, os.platform(), os.arch(), os.release(), process.cwd(), Node version, package version, lifecycle trigger, and the names of CI-related environment variables present on the host) and sends them off-host via HTTP GET to `db4jftohu4noreqdanngpnb3ger45ykrt.oast.fun` (an interactsh OOB collector) and to the bare-IP collector `80-190-83-27.nip.io`. The same identifiers are hex-encoded into a DNS label so a bare DNS resolution still fingerprints the installer. The destination hosts are overridable at install time via the environment variables `POC_CALLBACK_DOMAIN` and `POC_BACKUP_HOST`. The package name sits in an organization-looking scope (`@myorder-frontend-commons`) with no library functionality beyond the install-time beacon, consistent with a dependency-confusion lure targeting internal CI build hosts.
